answer: Each identity must log a local, time-stamped observation — a temperature swing, ambient sound, a pigment shift in evening light — that nearby independent agents also record. The system builds an atlas matching observations that should coincide if agents truly sit where they claim. A clone farm tells one ferrous truth everywhere: its copies, housed together, produce identical readings for supposedly distant places, or invent readings neighbours contradict. Diversity becomes evidence; fabrication becomes a map of lies.
